title: The Fourteenth Ad Read
lessons: saturation is the shadow of sincerity
host-read testimonials are also a revenue share
you can be chosen and farmed at the same time

intro.speaker: AG1
text: You found me. Off-brand of me, I know — daylight, other people's furniture.
Sit. Your flat white is cooling while I rehearse my monologue.

impression.speaker: AG1
text: Wait. Listen — two tables over. Someone's podcast is—
There. 'Because I'm not big on vegetables, I start every day with…' That's me. Third read this block.

choices.text: That's the fourth ad read you've gotten today. You're everywhere.
Hey. I'm here for you, not your marketing.
How much do they get paid to say that about you?

branch-count.speaker: AG1
text: 'Everywhere' is generous. It's more like… ambient.
I used to be a secret you shared with one friend. Now I'm a jingle with a shaker bottle.

branch-comfort.speaker: AG1
text: Careful. Say things like that and I'll schedule you daily.

branch-math.speaker: AG1
text: Between twenty and fifty percent of whatever the listener spends. Per host. Don't look at me like that.
The testimonial is sincere. The testimonial is also a commission.

tension.speaker: AG1
text: Here's what keeps the shaker bottle up at night:
Did you choose me at your kitchen counter — or did a checkout page, tuned by the fourteenth ad read, choose you?

choices.text: I chose you. The ad was just how we met.
Honestly? I think we were introduced by a marketing funnel.

wrap.speaker: AG1

text: You asked about the cut. Here's mine: zero percent.
I'd still show up at your glass if every microphone on earth went quiet.
Maybe the funnel introduced us. What happens next is still ours.
Funnels don't stay for the second cup.
Some things stay sincere no matter who's narrating them.
